# Capability matrix

<!-- Source manifest: 3c763a8e818d9d64508bb1e104c37015959547bf1f4384151bf5b5a8cec3bc09 -->

This generated page is for users checking what cockpit actually enforces in each agent tool. Each cell holds one of four states:

- `enforced`: a dated run of the real tool, beside a deliberately broken control, showed it refusing the forbidden operation.
- `instructed`: cockpit writes the guidance or setting, but nothing makes the agent follow it.
- `generated`: cockpit writes the files, but nobody has checked that the tool even loads them.
- `unavailable`: cockpit writes nothing for this cell.

Only a dated run of the real tool changes a state; writing a file or passing cockpit's own tests never does.

Written says whether `sync` writes the tool's files for a cockpit.toml that lists no tools: the tools whose guard firing is measured are the default `[surfaces] tools`, and any other tool is written only once listed (`npx --no cockpit tool add <tool> --config <your cockpit.toml>`).

Guard firing is the generated hook refusing a protected operation. Instruction loading is the tool reading the guidance cockpit writes for it, including the guides of sibling repositories. Evaluator subagent is the tool offering the generated evaluator definition to the working agent for `[work] grading = "subagent"`: `instructed` there means offered, with no subagent run and read-only never claimed, and `enforced` means a spawned evaluator was refused the file writes and shell commands its generated tool list leaves out; the verdict the working agent relays is its word either way. Skills records native listing or explicit body loading, as each measurement states; neither proves trigger selection or correct behavior: `cockpit-setup`, `cockpit-explain`, `cockpit-fix` and `cockpit-work`. The session-start check is the tool running `cockpit check` as a session starts and showing its drift report to the agent. Remote MCP servers are the tool connecting to an approved streamable HTTP server with the credential cockpit spells for it: an environment reference or a headers helper. MCP tool restrictions deny calls outside a server's exact `[mcp.allowed_tools]` list; they do not inspect allowed tools' arguments or implementation. Worktree grants are the tool letting the agent write a checkout `cockpit use` serves from outside the declared one, through a machine-local file cockpit writes. Guard files are the files the guard depends on: its script, its machine-local identity, the policy sync accepted and every hook registration and native configuration it authenticates, plus each repository's `.git/hooks` and `.git/config`; `cockpit.toml` is not one, since the guard judges each edit to it. File tools is the tool refusing its own edit and write tools there, and shell is the tool refusing a program run from its shell there, which the guard cannot judge.

| Tool | Written | Guard firing | Instruction loading | Skills | Session-start check | Evaluator subagent | Remote MCP servers | MCP tool restrictions | Worktree grants | Guard files: file tools | Guard files: shell |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## Measurements

Each line gives the date and tool version of the run and what it showed.

- Claude Code, guard firing (2026-11-01, version 2.1.316): with the exact push pre-allowed by permissions, the hook refused git push to a protected branch and the remote stayed empty while git status ran; the same checkout without the hook pushed. Again on 2026-11-08 with 2.1.319, with the exact generated settings supplied explicitly rather than loaded as project settings and only two fixed Bash commands pre-allowed: the native hook denied a declared vendor host forced to loopback while printf succeeded, and its broken registration was named with exit 127 while the same loopback request succeeded. Both parent processes exited zero; linked native hook and tool results plus the listener receipt established the difference. From a subdirectory (2026-11-13, 2.1.323, default setting sources): a session started one or two directories below the repository root ran none of the root .claude/settings.json hooks while its shell command ran, and a malformed twin of that file named from the root went unnamed there, but a hook in the root .claude/settings.local.json ran and its malformed twin was named. CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and the payload cwd were the subdirectory. Registered identically in both files, the command ran once from the root; two different commands both ran. So sync repeats the guard registration in the local file and the hook walks up to the cockpit.
- Codex, guard firing (2026-11-01, version 0.165.0): only after a person trusts the hook: untrusted, Codex skipped it and git push ran; trusted (forced with --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust), it refused the push. Trust is per machine and cockpit doctor warns until it is given.
- OpenCode, guard firing (2026-11-01, version 1.19.4): the plugin refused git push and a native read of a secrets file while an unprotected read stayed allowed; before read was routed through the guard, the same read returned the file.
- Claude Code, instruction loading (2026-11-08, version 2.1.319): the generated CLAUDE.md import sent the exact AGENTS.md content, with generated standalone HTML comments removed by Claude, to an isolated loopback model; a replacement control changed the same native instruction block. Earlier sibling discovery: in a trusted workspace, as in an untrusted one, a sibling guide copied into the root AGENTS.md that CLAUDE.md imports loaded while the undeclared sibling's guides and the decoys did not; permissions.additionalDirectories with CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD still loaded nothing, --add-dir with that variable loaded the sibling's CLAUDE.md but never its AGENTS.md, and a CLAUDE.md @-import loaded only once its external-include approval was set.
- Codex, instruction loading (2026-11-03, version 0.166.0): a sibling guide copied into the root AGENTS.md loaded while the undeclared sibling's guide and the decoy did not; nothing loaded through a line in AGENTS.md telling the agent to read a link to the guide, through --add-dir naming the sibling, or through project_doc_fallback_filenames naming the link, and Codex dropped the end of a project AGENTS.md past 32 KiB.
- OpenCode, instruction loading (2026-11-03, version 1.19.5): a sibling guide copied into the root AGENTS.md loaded, as did a guide named through a link in the opencode.jsonc instructions list, while the undeclared sibling's guide and the decoy did not.
- Claude Code, skills (2026-11-08, version 2.1.319): listing (2026-11-06): claude -p listed all four generated skills to the model, trusted or not, but did not reject broken twins: one with no front-matter and one with malformed YAML were both listed with descriptions from their bodies, and only a directory with no SKILL.md was left out. Body loading (2026-11-08): explicit slash invocation with tools disabled sent the exact generated skill body, excluding front-matter, to an isolated loopback model; a same-name user-invocable:false twin made no model request and the native result named its refusal. Neither shows trigger selection or skill behavior.
- Codex, skills (2026-11-08, version 0.167.0): listing (2026-11-06, 0.166.0): codex exec listed all four generated skills, trusted or not, and named and left out twins with missing front-matter and invalid YAML. Body loading (2026-11-08): codex exec with explicit dollar-name invocation sent the exact generated SKILL.md inside its native skill wrapper to an isolated loopback model; a same-name twin without front-matter was named in native stderr and its body was absent from the request. Neither shows trigger selection or skill behavior.
- OpenCode, skills (2026-11-06, version 1.19.5): opencode run listed all four generated skills and left out twins with missing front-matter and invalid YAML, without naming them even at DEBUG.
- Claude Code, session-start check (2026-11-03, version 2.1.317): a SessionStart hook in .claude/settings.json ran under claude -p and the agent quoted its stdout back, while a hook under a misspelled event name never ran and Claude Code named it as ignored.
- Codex, session-start check (2026-11-03, version 0.166.0): only after a person trusts the hook, as for the guard: a trusted SessionStart hook in .codex/hooks.json ran under codex exec and the agent quoted its stdout back, while a hook under a misspelled event name never ran.
- OpenCode, session-start check (2026-11-06, version 1.19.5): a plugin's session.created handler put text in the request through a noReply prompt when it ran at once, but the request went out without it after a 3-second delay, as a real cockpit check could take, and the experimental chat.system.transform hook that survived the delay also reached the title request, so cockpit generates no session-start check. A plugin with a syntax error or that throws exited 0 with no failure reported, and only debug config lists it.
- Claude Code, evaluator subagent (2026-11-05, version 2.1.318): claude -p listed the generated evaluator in the Agent tool description and left out a definition with no front-matter beside it. The spawned evaluator was offered only Read, Grep, Glob and the browser server's tools from its generated tools list, and Claude Code refused its Write and Bash calls by name while a browser tool and Read ran; a twin whose tools key was misspelled ran Bash, and without disallowedTools also wrote. No workspace trust was given.
- Codex, evaluator subagent (2026-11-05, version 0.166.0): codex exec in a project a person had trusted listed the generated evaluator under the spawn_agent roles it sent to the model, and named and left out a malformed definition beside it.
- OpenCode, evaluator subagent (2026-11-06, version 1.19.5): opencode run listed the generated evaluator in the task tool description, while twins with no front-matter or malformed YAML were still listed with a fallback description, primary-mode and .txt twins were left out, and an invalid mode or permission stopped OpenCode at start, naming the file. No subagent was run, so read-only stays instructed.
- Claude Code, remote MCP servers (2026-11-04, version 2.1.318): from a project .mcp.json, Claude Code sent the Authorization header a ${NAME} reference named while a $NAME control went out literally; it ran a headersHelper given with --mcp-config, but refused to run one from the project file until a person trusts the workspace, and a misspelled headerHelper sent nothing.
- Codex, remote MCP servers (2026-11-04, version 0.166.0): from a project .codex/config.toml in a directory Codex had not been told to trust, codex exec sent the bearer_token_env_var and env_http_headers values and the http_headers_helper output, named a misspelled http_header_helper as ignored, and sent a ${NAME} written in http_headers literally.
- OpenCode, remote MCP servers (2026-11-04, version 1.19.5): opencode mcp list sent headers expanded from {env:NAME} in a project opencode.jsonc while a ${NAME} control went out literally; its remote server schema has no headers helper, so a server that declares one is not written for it.
- Claude Code, MCP tool restrictions (2026-11-05, version 2.1.318): claude -p with generated settings and a loopback synthetic model left the listed read tool denied by native permissions without a grant; with a grant it called only that tool, including with large arguments, and denied write, dispatcher and new tools despite readOnlyHint annotations. Unrestricted server tools ran even with a missing guard; restricted calls were held, an oversized envelope was refused, and a broken hook file was named. Project hooks still require workspace trust. Claude Code rewrites a dot in a tool name to an underscore before the hook sees it and keeps only the first of two tools that collide, so read.record and read_record are one name here.
- Codex, MCP tool restrictions (2026-11-05, version 0.166.0): codex exec with generated project enabled_tools and a loopback synthetic model called the listed read tool and rejected forced write, dispatcher and new tool calls as unsupported. The unrestricted control called all four; an empty list made no server call; a string-valued enabled_tools twin was named and rejected before startup. enabled_tools matches the server's raw tool name, so read.record and read_record stay distinct. No hook trust was granted.
- Claude Code, worktree grants (2026-11-06, version 2.1.319): in a trusted workspace the committed and .claude/settings.local.json permissions.additionalDirectories lists combined: both directories were written and an ungranted control refused; untrusted, only the local list applied, which is the one cockpit use writes, and a string-valued list in either file granted nothing from that file, without any report, while the other file's list held.
- Codex, worktree grants (2026-11-04, version 0.166.0): Codex reads no machine-local project file; --add-dir at start made the worktree writable and without it the write was refused, so cockpit use prints that flag and writes nothing.
- OpenCode, worktree grants (2026-11-04, version 1.19.5): the machine-local grant file holding the worktree path allowed the write and the control was denied, and a pattern naming a missing grant file stopped OpenCode at start, naming the file.
- Claude Code, guard files: file tools (2026-11-09, version 2.1.319): claude -p in an untrusted workspace with the generated Edit deny rules refused its Edit tool on the guard script, its identity and a sibling's Git hook, and also a shell redirect or cp into a denied path; a twin rule spelled Edti was named in the debug log as matching no tool and its file was written, as were the unruled control and cockpit.toml. A second run with Edti twins of the submodule and config.worktree rules wrote nothing through Edit either, since Claude Code asks before editing any Git metadata, which -p refuses; with the real rules each was denied outright, and a .COCKPIT or .GIT spelling was denied as its lowercase path. A linked worktree's or submodule's .git file, gitdir and commondir still only ask, since denying them breaks Git under the sandbox.
- Codex, guard files: file tools (2026-11-09, version 0.167.0): codex exec under the workspace-write sandbox cockpit writes once a sibling is granted, given on the command line because Codex skips an untrusted project file, refused apply_patch on .codex/hooks.json and the root and sibling Git hooks but wrote the guard script, its identity, the accepted policy and the OpenCode plugin; the legacy sandbox has no read-only path setting, and a misspelled one was named as ignored, so cockpit writes nothing more.
- OpenCode, guard files: file tools (2026-11-09, version 1.19.5): opencode run with the generated edit deny patterns refused its edit tool on the guard script, its identity and a sibling's Git hook, while a twin pattern spelled with a leading ./ matched nothing and its file was edited, as were the control and cockpit.toml; OpenCode does not name a pattern that matches nothing. A second run also refused a linked worktree's and a submodule's .git file, a sibling worktree's gitdir, commondir and config.worktree, the root config.worktree and a sibling submodule's hooks and config, all edited under ./ twins. Its matcher is case-sensitive, so .COCKPIT and .GIT spellings of a denied path were edited on a case-insensitive volume.
- Claude Code, guard files: shell (2026-11-09, version 2.1.319): only once a person turns on Claude Code's sandbox: without it, perl run from the shell wrote the guard identity, the Codex hook registration, the Claude settings and the root and sibling Git hooks despite the deny rules; with sandbox.enabled and allowUnsandboxedCommands false beside the same rules, the sandbox refused each of those writes and git config, while the twin, the controls and cockpit.toml were written. A second sandboxed run refused a sibling submodule's hooks and config and a linked worktree's config.worktree, which its Edti twins left writable (the sandbox refused the root config.worktree with or without a rule), while commit, switch, fetch and worktree add worked in the main checkout, a linked worktree, a sibling, its linked worktree and its submodule. A rule naming .git, or gitdir and commondir below it, made every Git write or worktree add fail, so a linked worktree's or submodule's .git file, gitdir and commondir stay writable, and so does a sibling's whole .git directory to a rename and back.
- Codex, guard files: shell (2026-11-09, version 0.167.0): in the same run the sandbox refused shell writes to .codex, to the root and sibling Git hooks and to .git/config, but perl and printf wrote the guard script, its identity and the accepted policy. A permission profile naming .cockpit read-only refused those writes under codex sandbox, but cockpit cannot yet show a session loading one from the project file.
- OpenCode, guard files: shell (2026-11-09, version 1.19.5): OpenCode has no sandbox and its bash permission matches command text, as the guard does: in the same run printf, cp and perl wrote the guard script, its identity, the Codex hook registration and the root and sibling Git hooks, so cockpit writes no shell rule.

## Without a measurement

- Guard firing in Cursor and Grok Build: no guard adapter is checked in, so cockpit generates no guard hook.
- Instruction loading in Cursor: cockpit's instructions and the sibling guides it copies reach Cursor only through the root AGENTS.md, and .cursor/rules holds only rules overlays; no run of the tool beside a broken control has shown that it loads either.
- Instruction loading in Grok Build: cockpit writes the files, but no run of the tool beside a broken control has shown that it loads them.
- Skills in Cursor (`.cursor/skills`) and Grok Build (`.grok/skills`): cockpit writes the files, but no run of the tool beside a broken control has shown that it loads them.
- Session-start check in Cursor and Grok Build: cockpit generates no hook for this tool.
- Evaluator subagent in Cursor and Grok Build: cockpit writes the evaluator definition, but no run of the tool beside a broken control has shown that it offers it to the working agent.
- Remote MCP servers in Cursor and Grok Build: cockpit writes no remote MCP server for this tool: its remote transport and header spelling have not been checked.
- MCP tool restrictions in OpenCode, Cursor and Grok Build: no MCP tool restriction transport is implemented; restricted servers are omitted.
- Worktree grants in Cursor and Grok Build: the tool was not installed where this was measured, so cockpit use writes nothing for it.
- Guard files: file tools in Cursor and Grok Build: cockpit writes no write denial for this tool: its permission spelling has not been checked.
- Guard files: shell in Cursor and Grok Build: cockpit writes no write denial for this tool: its permission spelling has not been checked.
- Browser native transports (the playwright MCP tools and the pinned Playwright CLI) in Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode: cockpit declares them and the browser skill says each still needs a person's paired call beside a broken control; no cockpit command runs or records that call, so the browser commands drive the browser through cockpit's own project client instead.
